clue.text: Valiant he would be to reform the monstrous beast

indicators.note: to reform something is to reshape it, so the letters of these two words are made over into a new order

explanation.surface: A brave man would set out to reform a savage creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reform' shuffles VALIANT HE; 'would be' is only a link. The surface suggests a hero taming a beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The Leviathan is the huge sea monster of the Bible, so the word names any monstrous creature.

clue.text: Book-keeper good for a reference, perhaps?

definitions.text: Book-keeper good for a reference, perhaps?

parts.words: Book-keeper good for a reference, perhaps?
parts.note: not an accountant but someone who keeps books on shelves and helps readers look things up

explanation.walkthrough: 'Book-keeper' suggests accounts; read literally it is the person who looks after a library's books and its reference section.
explanation.definitionFit: A librarian looks after a collection of books and answers readers' reference enquiries.

clue.text: Vessels indispensable at first in a European uprising

indicators.note: in places the opening letter inside the reversed European
in a down clue uprising means reading the word upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a Slav is a European of the Slavic peoples

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of indispensable

explanation.surface: Vital equipment is needed at the start of an uprising in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' turns SLAV to VALS; 'in' puts I (from 'indispensable at first') inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Vials are small glass containers for liquids.

clue.text: Gangster supplying weapons — causing panic

parts.note: Al Capone was the famous Chicago gangster
arming means supplying with weapons

explanation.surface: A mobster arming people creates widespread fear.
explanation.walkthrough: AL, from Al Capone, is the stock crossword gangster.
explanation.definitionFit: Something alarming frightens or worries people.

clue.text: Semi-technical word for a short holiday

parts.note: semi means half
a term is a word with a specialised meaning

explanation.surface: Looks like a dictionary entry for a jargon word meaning a brief break.
explanation.walkthrough: Half-term is the short school holiday in the middle of a British school term.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the mid-term school break of about a week is called by this name.

clue.text: Essential quality Landor loved more than Art

definitions.meaning: Walter Savage Landor wrote: I loved this first, and next to it, Art

explanation.definitionFit: Nature means inherent character, and Landor's poem Dying Speech of an Old Philosopher ranks it above Art.

clue.text: On abandoning an instrument, becomes a singer

indicators.note: abandoning means the word on is left out of the instrument's name

parts.note: the bassoon is a woodwind instrument

explanation.surface: Someone gives up playing an instrument and turns to singing instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On abandoning' tells you to drop ON from BASSOON; 'becomes' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A basso is a bass singer, the lowest male voice in opera.

clue.text: Cloaked avenger's personal servant

definitions.meaning: the caped comic-book crime-fighter of Gotham City
an officer's orderly in the British Army

explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to the caped superhero, and also to an army officer's servant.

clue.text: There's space yet remaining for the housekeeper's stores

parts.note: still means yet, as in still remaining
room means space

explanation.surface: There's still space left for the housekeeper to put things away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There's' and 'for' only link. A stillroom was the room in a big house where preserves, cakes and drinks were kept and made.
explanation.definitionFit: In a large country house the stillroom held preserves and drinks under the housekeeper's charge.

clue.text: Stops being associated with this journal?

definitions.text: Stops being associated with this journal?

parts.words: Stops being associated with this journal?
parts.note: the instrument with pipe stops, which is also a word for a newspaper or periodical

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stops' looks like a verb but means the knobs that control the pipes; the same word names a publication, the mouthpiece of a party.
explanation.definitionFit: The church instrument has stops, and the word also means a periodical serving as a mouthpiece.

clue.text: American lawyer in affray case using boring device

indicators.note: in places the lawyer's letters inside the word for the fight

parts.note: an affray is a public fight, a case of one being a brawl
DA is a District Attorney, a US prosecutor

explanation.surface: A US attorney uses a drilling tool in a court case about a street fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the lawyer inside the fight. 'boring' sounds like 'dull', but here it means making holes.
explanation.definitionFit: A bradawl is a small hand tool that pierces holes in wood for screws.

clue.text: Initially the intended object of ten old householders

indicators.note: Initially takes the opening letter of each of the words the and intended

parts.note: an object is a thing

explanation.surface: Reads like a historian defining what ten old householders were meant to be.
explanation.walkthrough: In Anglo-Saxon England a tithing was a group of ten households answerable together for keeping the peace.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithing was a medieval unit of ten householders jointly responsible for each other's conduct.

clue.text: A service rejected in the Brahmaputra valley?

indicators.note: rejected is read as thrown back, so the word for the service is written backwards

parts.note: Mass is a church service

explanation.surface: A church service is turned away somewhere along a great Indian river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns the service round. The question mark marks a definition by example: the Indian state the Brahmaputra flows through.
explanation.definitionFit: Assam is the north-east Indian state lying mainly in the valley of the Brahmaputra river.

clue.text: Old sailor made King in Laputa

indicators.note: made is read as made up or fashioned, so these letters are put into a new arrangement

parts.note: R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A veteran seaman is crowned king on the flying island of Laputa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' mixes R, IN and LAPUTA. Laputa is the flying island in Gulliver's Travels.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarpaulin, like tar, was old slang for a seaman, from the tarred canvas sailors wore.

clue.text: Soldiers under eighteen going to the line

parts.note: in law a person under eighteen is an infant, a minor
RY is short for railway, a line

explanation.surface: Underage recruits are sent to the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going to' only joins the pieces. 'the line' looks military but is the railway abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Infantry are foot soldiers, the troops who fight on foot.

clue.text: Abandoned in infancy and discovered by a girl

definitions.text: Abandoned in infancy and discovered by a girl

parts.words: Abandoned in infancy and discovered by a girl
parts.note: a deserted baby picked up by someone, the word built as discovered plus a diminutive ending

explanation.walkthrough: The word splits as FOUND (discovered) plus the diminutive -LING; the girl is just the finder in the story.
explanation.definitionFit: A foundling is a deserted infant that someone has picked up and cared for.

clue.text: Resonant sound useful in filming

definitions.meaning: a deep, echoing noise such as thunder
a long pole that holds a microphone over actors on a film set

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a deep reverberating noise, and also the movable pole carrying a microphone in film and TV work.

clue.text: Set game — Anne's in her element

indicators.note: set is read as arranged or placed in order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the name with the s kept as a letter

explanation.surface: A game is set up, and Anne is in her element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' rearranges GAME ANNES; 'in her' only links. 'in her element' is an idiom for being happy.
explanation.definitionFit: Manganese is a metallic chemical element, number 25.

clue.text: Games counter contents always make us excited

indicators.note: contents means the word for always fills the inside of the counter

parts.note: a fish was a flat counter or token used in card games
ever means always

explanation.surface: Counting up in games always gets people worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contents' puts always inside the counter; 'make us' only links. A fish was a bone or ivory gaming token.
explanation.definitionFit: Feverish means wildly excited or agitated, as if with a fever.

clue.text: Claim to be thorough, if unseemly

parts.note: someone claiming to be something says I'm, short for I am
proper can mean thorough, as in a proper mess

explanation.surface: Insisting on being thorough could look unseemly.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as I'M PROPER: 'Claim to be' gives I'M and 'thorough' gives PROPER; 'if' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Improper behaviour is indecent or not in keeping with good manners.

clue.text: The opposite of 18. this word, when it's 28

definitions.text: The opposite of 18. this word, when it's 28

parts.words: The opposite of 18. this word, when it's 28
parts.note: the reverse of 18 (unseemly) gives proper, and a country's name like 28 is a proper part of speech, the naming kind

explanation.walkthrough: 18 is IMPROPER, so its opposite is PROPER; 28 is NIGER, a name, so it is a proper noun. The clue reads PROPER plus this word.
explanation.definitionFit: A naming word is the grammatical class that a country's title like Niger belongs to, specifically the proper kind.

clue.text: Male employee of old railway employed as course director

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
the LMS was the London, Midland and Scottish Railway, a British company of 1923 to 1947
a man can mean a worker or employee

explanation.surface: A former railwayman gets a job steering a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'employed as' only links. 'course' is a ship's heading, not a lesson plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A helmsman steers a vessel, directing the course it takes.

clue.text: Cut mane of horse — and upset soldiers?

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the person who cuts hair

parts.note: a barb is a Barbary horse from North Africa

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the soldiers' letters read backwards

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: Trimming a horse's mane might upset the cavalry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' only links and 'upset' turns the soldiers upside down. The definition is loose: a mane joked about as a head of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A barber is the hairdresser who trims hair and beards.

clue.text: Poles supported this house of Nokomis

definitions.text: Poles supported this house of Nokomis

parts.words: Poles supported this house of Nokomis
parts.note: not Polish people but tent poles holding up the home of Hiawatha's grandmother in Longfellow's poem

explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' tempts towards Poland, but means wooden stakes. Nokomis, Hiawatha's grandmother in Longfellow's poem, lived in such a dwelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A wigwam is a Native American dome-shaped hut of bark or hides on a pole frame.

clue.text: Madman baled out with small child

indicators.note: out is read as unsettled or disordered, so the letters of baled are rearranged

parts.note: a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: A lunatic bales out of an aircraft with a toddler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges baled into BEDLA. 'baled out' looks like a parachute jump.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bedlamite was an inmate of Bedlam, the old London asylum, hence a lunatic.

clue.text: Counter-acting joint

parts.note: a bar is a counter where drinks are served
on means acting or performing, as in on stage

explanation.surface: Reads as a joint that acts against something, a counteracting hinge.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen splits 'counteracting' into Counter + acting. A baron of beef is a large joint of two sirloins.
explanation.definitionFit: A baron of beef is a big roasting cut made of both sirloins left joined.

clue.text: Drink sailor knocked back in dance

parts.note: rum is a spirit, a drink

indicators.note: knocked back is read as sent backwards, so the sailor's letters are reversed

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor downs his drink at a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' looks like drinking, but it reverses the sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance.

clue.text: Profit commonly made from fruit

definitions.meaning: slang for a windfall share of profits
a large juicy fruit of the gourd family

explanation.definitionFit: In US slang a melon is a big bonus or dividend to share; it is also a round sweet fruit.

clue.text: Cockney artist's colourful exhibition

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist; the 's is read as is
a true Cockney is born within earshot of Bow Bells, so one is in Bow, an East London district

explanation.surface: A London painter puts on a bright show.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Cockney artist's' as 'an artist is in Bow': RA IN BOW. Bow is a district of London's East End.
explanation.definitionFit: A rainbow is a vivid arc of colours displayed across the sky.

clue.text: Sudden temptation to buy large quantity of beans?

definitions.meaning: an urge to purchase on the spur of the moment, as in a shop's checkout display
whimsically read as a big pulse, since beans and lentils are pulses

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a joke, marked by the question mark: beans are pulses, so a mighty helping might be called this.
explanation.definitionFit: An impulse is a sudden urge to act, as in impulse buying; pulses are edible seeds like beans.

clue.text: Northern Ireland boy returning to the Republic

indicators.note: returning means the boy's name is read backwards

parts.note: Reg is a boy's name, short for Reginald

explanation.surface: An Ulster lad heads back to the Irish Republic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses the boy. 'the Republic' suggests Ireland, but it is the West African state.
explanation.definitionFit: Niger is a landlocked republic in West Africa.

clue.text: A name Hera adapted for an Asian princess

indicators.note: adapted means altered, so the letters of these words are reworked into another order

explanation.surface: The goddess Hera's name is changed to suit an Indian royal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapted' shuffles A NAME HERA.
explanation.definitionFit: A maharanee is the wife or widow of a maharajah, an Indian queen or princess.
